source_first_claims.source_native_proposition: 25 volunteers enrolled; 3 excluded for fMRI head motion; original fMRI analysis n22 and df21
Four oriented Gabor items presented 2.4 sec each (9.6s total), delay4.8s, recall-cue 3/4 trials vs rest no manual response on1/4, 72 trials split2 scanner runs

source_first_claims.original_source: main p4 Fig2 p15 and original S6 p1
source_first_claims.source_native_proposition: Actual experimental set 14 distinct no-item-repeat four-element permutations (2 repeated sequences, 12 trial-unique), counterbalanced order with Hamming dissimilarity criterion>=3; do not equate 256 illustrative space
Two repeated exact sequences each practiced 12 times before fMRI; across 72 trials approximately 2/3 repetitions and 1/3 novel; experiment designed near-disjoint high-level chunks

source_first_claims.original_source: main p3 Fig1 and p5 Fig3
source_first_claims.source_native_proposition: Original target contrasts two rival internal sequence learner explanatory classes: frequency/count based associative code with shared item representations versus newly inferred n-gram chunk code, rather than solely measuring overall behavior
Classical associative item-position representation maps item category to ordinal slot, retains code identity while Dirichlet-multinomial posterior updates association counts/weights
Distinct associative item-item model uses adjacency or bi-gram n-gram overlap, not necessarily same item-position mechanism; original both comparator RDMs required

Alternative item-mixture control blends four item representations using configurable recency/primacy gradient; equal absolute slope yields same RDM so original RSA does not identify gradient temporal direction
Recoding model θ represents inferred higher-order observed co-occurrence as latent chunks x (n-grams) plus constituent mapping sequences z; not all combinations are brain-proven actual chunks
Prior probability of chunk n-gram length k inversely proportional to number of partial permutations of four distinct items at length k, penalising larger chunks with more combinations
Set of chunk codes x assigned independent multiplicative constituent n-gram priors, conditional assumption in source model
Sequence mapping z enumerates original eight possible partitions of a 4-item sequence, link probability fixed η and mapping probability η^F, product over individual sequences
Original prior for complete chunk model factorizes p(x,z|θ) into code probability and mapping probability; distinct code-versus-encoding complexity sources

source_first_claims.original_source: main p22-23 original Fig8 and Eq20 official S3 pp1–3
source_first_claims.source_native_proposition: Original Bayesian optimal chunk search uses model evidence and constrains candidate model set to EXACT observed-sequence encodings; original paper reports selected complexity tradeoff not blind comparison with noisy poor-fitting models
Source S3 shows p(θ|D) proportional to evidence p(D|θ) with uniform prior p(θ) across candidate chunk models; MAP based on exact-fitting candidate evidence.

At scan start after 12 training presentations each two repetitions, optimal inferred code is two four-grams; each novel highly dissimilar sequence encoded via original four uni-grams under source design and repeated chunks retained across trials

A fixed pure four-gram strategy eventually diverges from adaptive optimal encoding as novel sequences arrive; optimal chunk model has retained two trained four-grams plus uni-gram novelty, not each newly observed novel chunked as fresh four-gram

source_first_claims.original_source: main p5 Fig3 pp17–19 and p24 Eq21–23
source_first_claims.source_native_proposition: The original competing model predictions are representational dissimilarity matrices: item-position Hamming distance, item-item n-gram overlaps, mixture correlation distance, and source-optimal chunk constituent distances; compare ranked neural voxel RDM by Spearman correlation

fMRI RSA noise ceiling estimated per participant against group mean, including lower leave-self-out bound; original item-mixture acts alternative null against one undifferentiated superposition explanation

source_first_claims.original_source: main p25 and original S1 p1
source_first_claims.source_native_proposition: Original source imposes 3-way source significance criterion: model correlation greater than noise ceiling lower bound, positive lower bound, item-mixture null not at noise ceiling; no purely univariate total BOLD test
74 ROI × three presentation/delay/response task phases, correction α=.05/74/3 roughly 10^-4; response phase only 3/4 of trials; source region tests multiplicity controlled
Recoding RDM significant in exactly 3 reported named cortical ROIs and ONLY stimulus presentation phase; delay and response not significant for this source result

source_first_claims.original_source: main p8 Table1 and publisher S1 pp1-2
source_first_claims.source_native_proposition: Novel-only item-position representation fits in 11 regions in at least one task phase, which does NOT imply repeating learned sequences share item-position code in all11.

source_first_claims.original_source: main p8 plus p25 and S1
source_first_claims.source_native_proposition: Original authors report no significant cross novel-to-repeating item-position evidence under source-specific test, while novel-only item-position exists; original n22 and defined power/null scope
Proportion correctly recalled was .96 novel vs .97 repeating with no significant difference p=.22 for analyzed n22; original source repeats and novel both STM-length 4
Manual keypress intervals .552s novel vs .534s repeating difference -.018s with paired t=-3.04, p=.007; not model-class diagnostic by itself
Repeated sequences lower average univariate BOLD in several regions, which original notes both statistical learning mechanisms predict; no class identification from activation magnitude alone

source_first_claims.original_source: main p10 model-free analysis and Fig9 p27
source_first_claims.source_native_proposition: No measured within/among trained or novel pattern distance temporal slopes significant across participants in source model-free tests; these are NOT the cross-condition RSA outcomes

Worked equal-weight item-position case ABCD and BADC mistakenly boosts ABDC and BACD under this model, conditional interference example rather than mathematical proof against all possible associative sequence algorithms
Original Fig7 theoretical all 4-position possible strings N256 ALLOWING repeated items whereas actual observed stimuli 14 distinct four-item permutations; denominator must never merge

Source single item-position code interference reaches illustrative effective ~5 overlapping learned sequences within its own model; flexible bi-gram or higher chunk code can reduce expected shared parts, not general cortical capacity bound

source_first_claims.original_source: published S5 pp1-2 plus main p25
source_first_claims.source_native_proposition: Noise detectability simulation assumes model representation-noise reduction proportional to observed manual RT difference and uses pilot physiological fMRI noise estimates; only conditional sensitivity evidence
Original recency versus primacy item mixtures can have same absolute-slope RDM, making direction not identifiable with these pairwise distances; controls not extra invented learning stage
Published S1 FigA gives original per-region and phase novel-only comparator bars and noise ceiling, not original result that all n74 regions support recoding

Exactly fourteen four-item order strings recorded in original S6 including condition-dependent repeated identity counterbalance; synthetic 256 strings from interference section are NOT collected actual scan trials

Pre-existing visual Bayesian chunk evidence Orban et al 2008, Bayesian word segmentation Goldwater 2009 and RSA Kriegeskorte 2008 are direct methodological/concept ancestors; original 2021 work tests new source task and neural RSA not first invention of Bayesian chunks

Experimental scanner, Gabor program, recall cues, ROI preprocessing, hemodynamic model, group permutation testing are external World/Experiment relative to source candidate internal associative/chunk representation

Authors interpret evidence as chunk recoding for this short visual task within limited ROIs, not direct single-neuron chunk recording or universal mechanism shared by all tasks/species/neural networks

original_source_objections.source: Original publisher main p23 Fig8B Eq20 and actual mathematically main p22, official S3 p2-3
original_source_objections.finding: Same optimal structural CHUNK SET over designed trial stream is not identical to unchanged exact cumulative model evidence, which decreases as data accrue. Main Fig8B says initial pure-fourgram solution equals optimum at start but on new novel streams new fourgram-per-novel alternative diverges. A16/17 distinguish structure but do not state log model evidence is trial-dependent and decreasing.

original_source_objections.source: Main publisher original p25 original associative-noise RSA three possible branches, S5 both pages independently exact publisher
original_source_objections.finding: Source main says cross novel-vs-repeating Hamming RSA correlation non-significant means source lower-noise comparison is meaningless, as only when positive signal can one assess ν_N > ν_R. Its absence rejects source specified coding model in given ROIs but does NOT quantify all latent biological associative plasticity. S5 simulated detectability under 2 pilot fMRI noise profiles and response-time proportional assumed representation noise, not universal proof all nulls adequately powered.

original_source_objections.source: Original main publisher PDF p24–25 ROI×phase significance and S1 original p1 three-way criteria
original_source_objections.finding: A21 approximate threshold ~1e-4 omits exact unrounded alpha=.05/(74*3)=.000225225...; original source itself prints approx 10^-4 as order of magnitude. Preserve exact test denominator and don't overstate original reports p<10^-4 as exact Bonferroni formula; S1 triple criteria lower ceiling positive, item mixture null below ceiling.

original_source_objections.source: Publisher S3 p1–3 actual model evidence and exact-data-fitting subspace
